fields.h1: Build a Landscaping Quote Form That Arrives Ready to Price
fields.hero_description: Build a landscaping quote form that asks for the service, the address, the area, and yard photos, saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Estimator Knows Before Calling Back
fields.features_subheading: A landscaping quote form built with Emergent gathers the job details an estimator would otherwise measure on site.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that change with the service

Pick mowing and the form asks for the lawn size and how often to cut. Pick a retaining wall and it asks for the length, the height, and what sits behind it, like a slope.
fields.feature_2:
Yard photos sent with the request

Customers add yard photos from a phone while they fill in the form. The photos stay attached to the request, so the estimator sees the slope and the old beds before calling.
fields.feature_3:
A price on screen for routine work

Set a rate for mowing, mulch, or leaf cleanup, and the form works out the price from the size entered. The customer sees it before submitting, and it is saved with the request.
fields.feature_4:
Large jobs sent to the estimator

Name the jobs that need a visit, such as walls over 3 feet tall. Those requests show no price and email the estimator instead, photos included, to book a site visit.
fields.feature_5:
Requests saved in a database you own

Each request becomes a row with the service, the address, the size, the price shown, and its status. Filter by status to see which quotes are still waiting on a reply.
fields.feature_6:
The code, in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the code for the form and its quote table to your GitHub repository. Host it on your own servers, or hand it to a developer to keep building on.

fields.usecase_heading: Lawns, Walls, HOA Grounds, and Fall Cleanup
fields.tab_content_1:
With the lawn size entered, the season price appears

Fernside Lawn Care charges $55 a visit for any lawn up to 8,000 square feet. Talia Vennholt picks weekly mowing and enters 7,200 square feet. Before she submits, the form shows $55 a visit and $1,540 for the 28-visit season, and her request is saved with both prices.
fields.tab_content_2:
Dante gets the photos when a wall tops 3 feet

Stonebrook Hardscapes asks for the wall's length and height, what sits behind it, and photos. Ivo Szarka wants a 40-foot wall, 4 feet tall, holding back a slope. Any wall taller than 3 feet shows no price on the form. Dante, the estimator, gets an email with Ivo's 3 photos and calls him to book a site visit.
fields.tab_content_3:
An HOA's four common areas arrive in one email

Hollyfield Grounds quotes yearly maintenance for homeowner associations. Renata Ruiz-Abad manages Quillmere Commons and adds each common area as a row with its acreage. The entrance, clubhouse lawn, pond trail, and playground come to 3 acres. Wes Tollefsen, the account manager, gets all four in one email.
fields.tab_content_4:
At 7 days, Greta calls about any open quote

Tansley Landscape sent 20 fall cleanup quotes in October. Customers accepted 14, and 6 are still open. Any quote open more than 7 days goes on Greta's call list, and 4 are on it today. The Duquette yard is first, open 12 days.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Landscaping Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to create a landscaping quote form that prices routine work on screen and routes big jobs to an estimator.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down the services you quote
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the area in square feet
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide which jobs show a price
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for photos of the yard
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every service you price, such as mowing, mulch, leaf cleanup, and retaining walls. Each one becomes a choice in the first question and opens its own follow-up questions. Leave out the work you never take on.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the lawn or bed size in square feet. For customers who don't know it, add a hint: pace off the length and width, then multiply. Put the property address and a callback number on the same screen.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each routine service a rate, like one price per visit for lawns up to a set size. Work you need to see first, such as a tall wall or a drainage problem, shows no price and goes to your estimator.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Request a photo from the street and another from the back of the property. A slope or a narrow side gate shows up in the request before anyone drives out to look at it.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the services and their rates into one prompt, along with the jobs that go to your estimator. Emergent builds the landscaping quote form, the database behind it, and a screen listing every request. Change a rate later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Track every quote until it closes
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give each request a status, open or accepted, and the date the quote went out. Then pick the number of days after which an open quote moves to your call list. Start with 7 days.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Submit a test request from a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form on a phone at the curb, with photos of your own yard. Check that a mowing request shows its price, and that a tall wall reaches the estimator's inbox with the photos attached.

faq_plan.q: What is a landscaping quote form?
faq_plan.a: A landscaping quote form is the online form a customer fills in to ask a landscaping company for a price. It collects the service wanted, the property address, and the size of the area. Yard photos come with it when the crew needs to see the site before naming a number.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a landscaping quote form?
faq_plan.a: List the services you quote, the rate for each routine job, and which jobs need a visit first. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, and you change a rate or a question later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a landscaping quote form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with the service, the property address, and how many square feet need work. Then ask what that service needs: how often to mow, how long and tall a wall should be, or how many beds need mulch. End with photos and the best way to reach the customer.

faq_plan.q: Can a landscaping quote form show a price before the customer submits?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for work you price by size. Give each lawn size band a rate per visit, and the form shows the price as soon as the customer enters the square footage. Keep jobs you have to see in person off that screen. A cleaning quote form runs the same math on bedrooms and bathrooms instead of square feet.

faq_plan.q: How can customers find their lawn size on a landscaping quote form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the length and the width in feet, and let the form multiply them into square feet. Add a hint to pace off two sides of the yard if no tape measure is handy. Then add a Not sure option that sends the request to you, and measure it on the first visit.

faq_plan.q: Should a landscaping quote form require photos?
faq_plan.a: Require them for walls and drainage work, where the price depends on what the site looks like. Leave them optional for mowing, since the lawn size already sets the price. In a form built with Emergent, each photo lands in a database you own, in the same row as the address and the price shown.

faq_plan.q: Which jobs should a landscaping quote form send to a site visit instead of pricing?
faq_plan.a: Send any job whose price depends on something a photo cannot show, such as the soil behind a wall or the grade of a slope. Set the rule on the form, like walls over 3 feet tall, and those requests skip the price screen. A deck or a home addition belongs on a construction quote form instead.

faq_plan.q: Can a landscaping quote form price a full season of lawn care?
faq_plan.a: Yes: price one visit, then multiply it by the visits in the season. Let the customer pick weekly or every two weeks, and show the per-visit price next to the season total. Ask for the start date too. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, so a spring rush of requests never closes the form.

faq_plan.q: How do I follow up on quotes sent from a landscaping quote form?
faq_plan.a: Give every quote a status and the date it went out, then set a day count that moves open quotes to a call list. Call about the larger jobs first. The app can send you an email reminder each morning with every quote still open past that count.

faq_plan.q: What other forms go alongside a landscaping quote form?
faq_plan.a: Start with a work order and a service report, which take over once a quote is accepted. The crew gets a work order for each job and files a service report after each visit. When a youth league or a garden tour asks you to back it, a sponsorship form collects the event and the amount asked for in one place.
